articles.title: Últimos feriados 2026 en el Perú: ¿Cuántos feriados hay en noviembre y diciembre?
articles.summary: Conoce el calendario oficial de feriados en Perú para 2026 y revisa qué días libres quedan en los últimos meses del año. Consulta las fechas de noviembre y diciembre para planificar tus viajes, actividades familiares o próximos descansos.
articles.body_text: Con el final de ciertas celebraciones del año, muchos trabajadores y estudiantes ya empiezan a revisar el calendario para conocer cuál será el siguiente descanso oficial del año. Los feriados representan una oportunidad para planificar viajes, compartir tiempo en familia o simplemente hacer una pausa en la rutina, por lo que existe un gran interés en conocer las próximas fechas establecidas por ley. Además de permitir un espacio para el descanso, estas jornadas suelen generar un importante movimiento en sectores como el turismo, el comercio, la gastronomía y el transporte, debido al incremento de personas que aprovechan los días libres para salir de la ciudad o realizar diversas actividades. Del mismo modo, muchas empresas y entidades organizan con anticipación sus operaciones para adecuarse al calendario oficial, mientras que las familias aprovechan estas fechas para programar reuniones, escapadas de fin de semana o visitas a distintos destinos del país. Por ello, conocer con anticipación cuándo será el próximo feriado resulta clave para organizar la agenda personal y laboral, evitar contratiempos y sacar el máximo provecho a los días de descanso que aún quedan en el 2026. A continuación, te contaremos todo lo que debes saber sobre esta situación. Si quieres saber cuándo será el próximo feriado y qué fechas aún quedan por disfrutar este año, aquí te contamos todos los detalles. Los feriados son fechas establecidas por ley en las que los trabajadores tienen derecho a suspender sus labores sin que ello afecte su remuneración. Durante estas jornadas, el descanso es obligatorio tanto para el sector público como para el privado, salvo en aquellas actividades que, por su naturaleza, deben continuar operando. Si un trabajador presta servicios durante un feriado y no recibe un día de descanso compensatorio, la legislación laboral establece que le corresponde una remuneración adicional por haber laborado en esa fecha, conforme a las disposiciones vigentes. A diferencia del feriado, el día no laborable no constituye un descanso obligatorio para todos los trabajadores. Generalmente, esta medida se aplica al sector público con el objetivo de extender periodos de descanso o promover actividades como el turismo interno. En el caso de las entidades públicas, las horas que no se trabajan deben recuperarse posteriormente, dentro del plazo fijado por la normativa o según lo disponga cada institución. Para el sector privado, la aplicación de un día no laborable depende de un acuerdo entre empleador y trabajadores. Si no existe consenso sobre la recuperación de las horas, será el empleador quien determine la forma en que estas deberán compensarse.

articles.title: Voice AI in vogue: Nvidia releases new open transcription model | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Nvidia just released a free speech-to-text model that can transcribe up to 40 languages, but it only works on recordings, not live audio, so it’s a big step for meeting and medical transcription tools while still leaving real-time use to rivals like ElevenLabs.
articles.body_text: Nvidia on Wednesday released Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe , a free, open-weight model that transcribes audio in up to 40 languages. It also released version 2 of Granary, its open-source speech dataset. Nvidia boasts that Nemotron 3.5 can translate 31 languages to and from English, handle recordings up to an hour long, and tell up to eight speakers apart. It claims to beat rivals on benchmarks, including Hugging Face’s Open ASR Leaderboard . These tools target developers building apps for business meetings and medical transcription, two of AI’s most established footholds in the workplace. Nvidia says developers can use the model, the updated Granary dataset, and tools like its NeMo Speech model to customize apps to recognize an industry’s jargon in each language. One drawback: Transcribe works with recorded audio, not live streams. Still, the company promises Transcribe, at 30 billion parameters, can run on a single chip, from the Jetson AGX Thor robotics controller and DGX Spark chip powering new laptops , to Blackwell datacenter chips. It joins Nvidia’s open-weight voice models, including the super small yet powerful Parakeet (1.1 billion parameters). Nvidia’s latest voice entry comes during busy period of AI voice releases: Mistral shipped Voxtral 3 earlier this month; ElevenLabs launched Realtime for instant speech in voice agents; and Salesforce released Launa-Omni, its voice model. articles.title: Amazon debuts the Alexa Photo Frame and Echo Time smart clock, plus other upgraded devices | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Amazon's other new decides include an upgraded Echo Dot, an Echo Studio with visual intelligence features, and the Echo Show 16.
articles.body_text: Amazon unveiled five new Alexa devices today, including two new kinds of hardware: the Alexa Photo Frame , a smart picture frame, and the Echo Time, a smart alarm clock. The Alexa Photo Frame is Amazon’s foray into the world of digital photo displays, a product category that has transcended from a clunky, last-minute holiday gift to a sleek, attractive way to look through your camera roll. Aura is responsible for much of the growth in this category, so it’s no coincidence that the Alexa Photo Frame has a similar aesthetic feel: The screen is much easier on the eyes than the old, bright photo frames from years past. The device is said to be specifically calibrated for sharing photos, featuring a semi-matte, anti-glare display that makes it look more like a Samsung Frame TV than a laptop screen. Also like Aura, the Photo Frame’s 10-inch screen looks like matte photograph, helping it blend in with other artwork on your wall. Amazon’s new device, though, adds the value of integration with users’ existing Amazon accounts. Prime members get unlimited storage on Amazon Photos, and Alexa+ is supposed to intelligently choose how and when to display photos. “It knows to choose photos where you’re smiling and the lighting is right, and it matches the season you’re in, so you see last year’s family Halloween costumes in October instead of the middle of spring. It also knows what to skip, like screenshots and receipts,” Amazon said in a press release. You can also add voice notes to photos, and images sync automatically as you take them. The Alexa Photo Frame is on sale now , and starts at $199.99 in Black, and $229 in Birch or Walnut wood. Meanwhile, the Echo Time clock seems to be a response to the growing sentiment that people don’t want to rely on their phones for alarms, setting morning reminders or checking the weather. “Millions of customers start and end their days with Alexa—checking the weather and turning on the lights from bed in the morning or winding down with white noise at night,” Amazon wrote. “But the bedroom asks for something different from a device than the kitchen or living room does—so we designed an Echo specifically for it.” Amazon says that the Echo Time , which costs $199.99, or $209.99 for a Kids version, has opt-in sleep sensing tools. You can choose to set a smart alarm feature that wakes you up anywhere between 10 to 60 minutes of your alarm, and can wake you when it detects you’re in a lighter phase of sleep, so that it’s less jarring to begin your day. Like the popular Hatch alarm clocks, the clock can also mimic sunrise features to ease you awake. Amazon also showed off updates to its existing lines of devices. We now get the Echo Show 16, a new Echo Dot, and Echo Studio with Home Camera.

articles.title: Jio shares surge 21% in market debut after blockbuster India IPO | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Jio has debuted as India's second-most valuable listed company, behind its parent, Reliance Industries.
articles.body_text: The shares opened at ₹1,358 (about $14) apiece, up from their IPO price of ₹1,119 (around $12). That valued Jio at around ₹12.5 trillion (around $131.9 billion), making it India’s second-most valuable listed company after its parent, Reliance Industries, which is worth about ₹16 trillion (around $168.6 billion). In 2020, when Meta and Google invested, Jio was valued at up to ₹4.91 trillion ( about $65 billion at the time). In 2016, Jio entered what was then a crowded Indian telecom market, offering free data and low-cost services. That helped it quickly win customers from established operators including Bharti Airtel, Vodafone Idea, and state-owned BSNL. It has since become the country’s largest telecom operator. Akash Ambani (pictured above), Jio Platforms’ managing director, said at Wednesday’s listing ceremony that its platforms serve more than 540 million customers. Jio’s prices are now broadly in line with those of its rivals’, but its business has expanded into broadband , cloud services , and AI . Akash, Mukesh Ambani’s eldest son, has taken on a larger role in Jio as his father gradually hands more responsibility to the next generation of Reliance’s leadership. At the listing ceremony, he said he wants Jio to become a global technology company. “My dream is that one day, when the world counts its great technology companies, one of them will be from India, and that company will be called Jio Platforms Limited,” he said. Jio made ₹300.5 billion (about $3.2 billion) in profit on revenue of ₹1.47 trillion (around $15.5 billion) in the fiscal year ended March 2026, with both figures up about 15% from a year earlier. In the June quarter, Jio’s revenue grew nearly 12% and profit rose 9%. From the IPO proceeds, Jio plans to use up to ₹275 billion (about $2.9 billion) to repay debt at its telecom subsidiary, Reliance Jio Infocomm, with the remainder going toward general corporate purposes. Jio had total borrowings of ₹613.7 billion (around $6.5 billion) as of June 30. Jio drew billions of dollars from American investors during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020. Meta, then known as Facebook, invested $5.7 billion , while Google put in $4.5 billion . General Atlantic, Silver Lake, and Vista Equity Partners were among the other investors that backed the company. None sold shares in the IPO, which consisted entirely of newly issued shares. articles.title: VCs will make billions on Anthropic's IPO, but Amazon is set to make much (much) more | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Massive note conversions reveal the true extent of Amazon's ownership in Anthropic.
articles.body_text: Many investors stand to win big when Anthropic goes public. Stakes held by firms including Menlo Ventures, Sequoia, Sound Ventures, and Spark Capital are expected to return billions . Yet according to Anthropic’s S-1 , none of those VC firms owns 5%, the threshold for being included in the principal stockholders’ table. That’s highly unusual. In a typical tech IPO, lead venture investors hold double-digit-percentage stakes in the startups they backed. The reason is Anthropic’s size. At its $965 billion private valuation, a 1% stake is worth nearly $10 billion, so, for example, Menlo’s roughly $14 billion position is only about 1.5% of the company, according to recently reported Bloomberg figures. While the venture firms may lack sizable percentage stakes, Anthropic sold large stakes to strategic partners, companies that are also its business partners. Indeed, Amazon is likely the single largest financial beneficiary of the IPO. Amazon first backed Anthropic in 2023 with a commitment to invest up to $4 billion in the AI company. Since then, Amazon has poured billions more into Anthropic. Instead of taking stock upfront, Amazon structured much of its investment as convertible notes, a type of debt that converts into shares upon an IPO or sale. According to the S-1, Amazon holds convertible notes with $6.2 billion in principal outstanding as of June 30. That is Anthropic’s entire debt load. But as Anthropic’s valuation soared across successive funding rounds, the shares those notes will convert into became far more valuable. Amazon’s own filings valued its note holdings at $97.9 billion as of June 30. As the value of Amazon’s convertible notes surged, Anthropic had to record the growing value of what it owes on its books. It reported the adjustments on its income statement under “change in fair value of convertible notes, derivative liabilities, and SAFEs,” a line that totaled $72.4 billion for the first half of 2026. The charge is non-cash, meaning no money left the company. Amazon’s notes could convert into as many as 1.84 billion shares, according to the S-1. But a cap limits Amazon to 12% of Anthropic’s “partially diluted” share count, a figure that counts some shares not yet issued, such as stock options. Amazon can waive the cap. Notes that can’t convert will stay outstanding and convert in later quarters, subject to the same limit. But the notes are only part of Amazon’s holdings. It further invested $10 billion in nonvoting preferred stock (a type of equity), in the second quarter, according to Amazon’s quarterly report for the period ended June 30. Amazon did this by investing $5 billion in each of Anthropic’s last two funding rounds. Combined with the $8 billion it invested in the notes from 2023 through 2025, that brings Amazon’s total investment to about $18 billion. Beyond its stock gains, Amazon will also continue to earn significant revenue from Anthropic, which has committed to spend at least $110 billion on AWS over the next 10 years. Google, too, is set for a major windfall from both the listing and its cloud computing deals with Anthropic. The search giant held about 14% of Anthropic as of early last year, according to court filings that were reported by The New York Times , and has invested more since, including $10 billion in April. (Google was likely diluted in subsequent and massive funding rounds, with PitchBook analyst Harrison Rolfes telling TechCrunch he estimates its current stake at closer to 5.6%.) It has also secured at least $114 billion in cloud commitments from the Anthropic through 2033. While VCs set for massive paydays have little reason to complain, the S-1 makes it clear that the biggest winners of Anthropic’s IPO may well be tech giants like Amazon, which backed a would-be rival early on and now sell it much of the computing power it runs on. The S-1 itself warns that some of those cloud providers also build rival AI models and that they may not always want the same things that Anthropic does.

articles.title: The data center boom has an upside: innovation for the US grid | TechCrunch
articles.summary: As the AI boom stresses the existing power grid, all sorts of new opportunities for grid modernization are also emerging as a result, industry insiders say.
articles.body_text: The AI boom has led to a gargantuan surge in energy demand across the country. Critics say this upswell in connections is enacting a stress test on America’s aging grid infrastructure. Worries abound that, in the short term, the energy crunch could lead to surging electrical bills and, in the long term, may eventually lead to outages or other technical problems. At TechCrunch Disrupt earlier this month, industry insiders tempered much of this criticism with optimism about how the flood of new energy connections could actually be opening the door for grid modernization. Apoorv Bhargava, founder and CEO of WeaveGrid, Tim Heidel, CEO of Veir, and Kristin Eberhard, VP of policy at Rewiring America, said that though the grid faces new challenges, there are also plenty of new opportunities as well. “It’s a very different electric grid, right?” said Bhargava. “We’re dealing with a ton of new variables, including renewable energy. We’re dealing with a ton of new load in the form of electric vehicles and data centers and heat pumps, and the ability to manage and orchestrate is fundamentally what utilities are now grappling with.” While all of those new connections are driving an ever larger amount of stress to the grid, Bhargava’s company hopes to provide the kind of load orchestration and management that helps utilities maximize the potential of the current system. WeaveGrid’s software can help organizations efficiently deploy energy while also optimizing connections to reduce utility payers’ bills, the founder said. Heidel, on the other hand, runs a company that is working to build out and expand the physical infrastructure of the grid, while also making it run much more efficiently. Veir sells superconductive power lines that promise to transfer energy at a much more efficient rate than traditional ones. Veir’s cables can carry power five times farther than traditional cables while also requiring 20 times less space, the company has said . articles.title: GM is embracing hybrids now | TechCrunch
articles.summary: GM eschewed hybrids in favor of battery-electric vehicles. Now it's gearing up to offer hybrid versions of its SUVs.
articles.body_text: General Motors plans to invest in its Lansing Delta Township Assembly plant to handle future production of hybrid-electric vehicles, the latest move by the U.S. automaker to claw back market share by appealing to the shifting tastes of consumers. The company said on Tuesday that it plans to invest more than $2 billion over the next several years in the broader Lansing region, an amount that includes $1.25 billion to prepare the assembly plant for “future vehicle production.” The company said it is working with the U.S. Department of Energy to restructure a previously awarded Domestic Manufacturing Conversion Grant and direct those funds to future hybrid production at the Lansing factory. The company was awarded $500 million under the Biden administration to support converting a different factory in Lansing to produce electric vehicles, including hybrid, battery-electric, plug-in electric hybrid, and hydrogen fuel cell electric vehicles. Those funds were never released, according to GM. Today, GM assembles the gas-powered Buick Enclave, Chevrolet Traverse, and GMC Acadia at the Lansing Delta Township factory, which produced a record 291,000 vehicles in 2025. GM didn’t provide specifics on when it would begin producing and selling hybrid vehicles. But insiders told TechCrunch to expect hybrids across multiple brands rather than a single vehicle line. A Reuters report , citing anonymous sources, said the company plans to build hybrid versions of the Chevrolet Traverse, Buick Enclave, and GMC Acadia at the factory. Hybrids have become increasingly popular, thanks in part to rising gas prices. Customers also have more choices than ever before, with most automakers offering a range of hybrid and plug-in hybrid models. Toyota is the U.S. market leader in hybrid sales, followed by Honda. Ford has also gained considerable market share in hybrid sales in the past two years, selling some 228,000 hybrids in 2025. But GM has been slow to adopt hybrids. Until recently, the company’s only electric-hybrid vehicle was the Chevrolet Corvette E-Ray , which launched as a 2024 model. (GM sold 2,444 of those vehicles last year.) The E-Ray has since been discontinued; GM began deliveries of the hybrid Corvette ZR1X in March and next year will launch a hybrid Corvette Grand Sport X. GM eschewed hybrids in favor of battery-electric vehicles. The automaker invested billions of dollars to shift its gas-powered portfolio to an all-electric one. That strategy has changed under the Trump administration with the end of the federal EV tax credit and slower-than-expected demand. GM hasn’t abandoned EVs completely, though it has seen EV sales fall year-over-year. The company still sells numerous battery-electric vehicles across its brands, including the Chevrolet Equinox EV, Blazer EV, and Cadillac Escalade IQ. GM said Tuesday it will share specific details on its hybrid vehicle production plans closer to launch. When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission . articles.title: Bank of America kindly asks that you don't share your banking password with your AI assistant | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The banking giant reminds customers that "you're responsible for activity" resulting from your AI agents' access.
articles.body_text: Financial giant Bank of America is reminding customers to bank safely by kindly not sharing your banking credentials with your AI agent. In an email blast to customers titled “Protecting your finances in the Al World,” Bank of America urged customers to never share their username and password with another person or an outside service, “including an Al-enabled tool or agent that offers to act on your behalf.” You can practically sense the frustration in the person sending the email. Still, customers are increasingly handing over their log-ins as personal AI assistants grow more popular . Sharing your banking username and password with an AI assistant runs the risk that it could do something with your finances without your knowledge, or that your bank thinks someone’s raiding your account and locks you out of it. Worse, a security flaw in the AI assistant could result in it leaking your banking credentials elsewhere, giving financially motivated hackers a way into your bank account. This latest warning comes as banks are still exploring how AI agents fit into the financial world but are reportedly grappling with unauthorized agents accessing their customers’ money . As we discussed onstage at TechCrunch Disrupt , banks, payment providers, and processors are still trying to figure out how to allow customers access to their bank accounts using AI tools, such as for agentic payments, which allow people to set agents to autonomously buy things at the best price or the right time. A spokesperson for Bank of America confirmed the authenticity of the bank’s email that was posted to social media . But heed the bank’s warning, for if things go wrong, it’s on you. Account agreements at most banks hold customers responsible for anyone they give their log-in to. “If you do share your credentials,” its email reads, “keep in mind that you’re responsible for activity resulting from that access.” When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission . articles.title: Who's really in charge at Anthropic after the IPO? | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Here's a clear explanation of Anthropic's incredibly complex governance structure.
articles.body_text: Anthropic was founded in 2021 to ensure humanity can control AI and benefit from it in the long-term. As the frontier lab approaches its initial public offering, however, there’s one class of humanity that is being shut out of control: anyone who buys its stock on public markets. Complex structures that allow founders like Elon Musk or Mark Zuckerberg to control their public companies without owning most of them are nothing new in Silicon Valley. But Anthropic’s obsession with AI safety has resulted in a truly baroque style of corporate governance that will leave common shareholders with little say over most major decisions at the AI company, including who sits on its board. First, Anthropic is a public benefit company — a for-profit corporation legally allowed to weigh a public mission alongside profit — with the goal of promoting AI safety. That status protects the board’s ability to make decisions about AI safety that aren’t driven entirely by shareholder value without being sued by angry investors. Right now, the board is chaired by Anthropic president Daniela Amodei and includes CEO Dario Amodei (her brother), Netflix cofounder Reed Hastings, former Microsoft and GM CFO Christopher Liddell, Novartis CEO Vas Narasimhan, and Spark Capital partner Yasmin Razavi. There is one vacancy on the board. Second, Anthropic has allocated significant control of its board to a Long-Term Benefit Trust (LTBT), an independent panel meant to keep the company focused on mission to benefit humanity. The trust owns a class of stock that gives it the ability to elect and remove a majority of the company’s board, known as Class T directors. The LTBT is chaired by Neil Shah, a global health expert who was managing director at GiveWell, a nonprofit that ranks charities, and includes former Federal Reserve chair Ben Bernanke, national security expert Richard Fontaine, and Harvard physicist Christopher Stubbs. There is one vacancy on the LTBT right now. The existing members will themselves choose who fills it. Third, Anthropic’s seven founders also jointly own a special class of stock that gives a majority of them 50.1% of shareholder voting power, allowing them to elect three members of the board of directors. If, for whatever reason, there’s no majority among the founders, only then are their shares voted in proportion with holders of common stock. Finally, the board can put a check on the LTBT. When the LTBT nominates a “Specified” one of its four directors, or removes that director without cause (that is, without alleging misconduct), the board’s nominating committee can decline to approve the move and throw the decision to the company’s employees for a vote. The dynamics of such a complex structure are hard to predict. We’ve already seen one notable instance where a similar structure was essentially overthrown: OpenAI’s so-called blip, when OpenAI’s board briefly fired CEO Sam Altman over concerns that he was not being candid with them. Thanks to the loyalty of the company’s employees to Altman, the board backed down, reinstated him, and a new governance structure was put in place. Anthropic’s structure seems to formalize that kind of employee power. At Anthropic, cracks in the founders’ unified front could lead to common shareholders having more say than expected, while employees can overrule the LTBT on board seats if they back the board over the assembled luminaries. The founders’ control won’t last forever: Ten years after the IPO, the founders can choose to end their control of the company, or their control will end automatically when fewer than three of them remain. At that point, the LTBT will continue until 85% of common shareholders vote to end it, or it decides to step down with approval from the board. If and when neither special class of shareholder exists any more — hopefully not because of an AI-driven catastrophe — common shareholders finally get control. articles.title: Parents sue OpenAI over ChatGPT's role in son's suicide | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Before sixteen-year-old Adam Raine died by suicide, he had spent months telling ChatGPT about his plans to end his life.
articles.body_text: Before 16-year-old Adam Raine died by suicide, he had spent months consulting ChatGPT about his plans to end his life. Now, his parents are filing the first known wrongful death lawsuit against OpenAI, The New York Times reports . Many consumer-facing AI chatbots are programmed to activate safety features if a user expresses intent to harm themselves or others. But research has shown that these safeguards are far from foolproof. In Raine’s case, while using a paid version of ChatGPT-4o, the AI often encouraged him to seek professional help or contact a help line. However, he was able to bypass these guardrails by telling ChatGPT that he was asking about methods of suicide for a fictional story he was writing. OpenAI has addressed these shortcomings on its blog. “As the world adapts to this new technology, we feel a deep responsibility to help those who need it most,” the post reads . “We are continuously improving how our models respond in sensitive interactions.” Still, the company acknowledged the limitations of the existing safety training for large models. “Our safeguards work more reliably in common, short exchanges,” the post continues. “We have learned over time that these safeguards can sometimes be less reliable in long interactions: as the back-and-forth grows, parts of the model’s safety training may degrade.” These issues are not unique to OpenAI. Character.AI, another AI chatbot maker, is also facing a lawsuit over its role in a teenager’s suicide. LLM-powered chatbots have also been linked to cases of AI-related delusions , which existing safeguards have struggled to detect. articles.title: Apple is buying 20 percent of its iPhone satellite services partner
articles.summary: Apple is prepaying satellite provider Globalstar $1.1 billion to expand service for its iPhone Emergency SOS feature.
articles.body_text: Apple is taking a 20 percent stake in its iPhone satellite connectivity partner Globalstar — a stake worth $400 million — as part of an expansion of its deal with the company. Globalstar will also receive a prepayment of $1.1 billion from Apple that is intended to improve satellite infrastructure. Apple relies on Globalstar’s satellites to enable to send emergency text messages, iMessage reactions, and more through the skies in areas with no cell signal. Globalstar disclosed the details of the deal expansion in an SEC filing, which includes “a new satellite constellation, expanded ground infrastructure, and increased global [mobile satellite services] licensing.” Apple launched its Emergency SOS feature on the iPhone 14 in 2022 and expanded it with iOS 18, enabling off-grid users to send and receive texts, emoji, and Tapbacks over iMessage and SMS out in the wilderness. Apple intends to charge owners for satellite connectivity service at some point but still hasn’t. Starting with the iPhone 14, Apple has offered access to its satellite features for free two years with your phone. But last year, iPhone 14 owners were given an extra year, extending free service to as early as November 2025.

articles.body_text: Minst 64 människor har dött efter tågkraschen i Spanien. En av dem som överlevde var El Pais -reportern Antonio Jiménez Barca. ”Jag var täckt av blod. Jag hade människor ovanpå mig och det låg många personer runt omkring”, skriver han om kraschen. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Klockan var strax före 09 på onsdagen när två tåg kolliderade vid Toledo utanför spanska huvudstaden Madrid . En av dem som var ombord på ett av tågen var El País-reportern Antonio Jiménez Barca. I en text berättar han att hans tåg var stillastående i 10-15 minuter innan det kändes som att någon knuffade honom. ” Jag stod i början av restaurangvagnen och hamnade längst bak i den. Jag slog huvudet fruktansvärt hårt. ” Han beskriver hur han var helt täckt av blod och att det låg människor på och runt honom. Tillsammans med två andra personer lyckades han ta sig ut ur vagnen och ner på ett fält invid banvallen. De tre hjälpte andra resenärer att ta sig ut. ” Några av dem som hade befunnit sig i restaurangvagnen var allvarligt skadade, ” skriver Jiménez Barca. Men restaurangvagnen hade klarat kraschen förhållandevis bra, jämfört med tågets första vagn. ”Den var fullständigt sönderslagen och det låg människor utspridda längs slänten. Jag såg också en person som satt i en fåtölj mitt ute på fältet. Eller jag tror åtminstone att det var vad jag såg. ” Antonio Jiménez Barca och flera andra resenärer försökte hjälpa de skadade. De avlöstes allt eftersom av blåljuspersonal.

articles.title: Utvisades i natt
articles.summary: Under natten lyfte ett plan med somalier som fått utvisningsbeslut från Arlanda. Nu bekräftar migrationsminister Johan Forssell utvisningarna.
articles.body_text: Under natten lyfte ett plan med somalier som fått utvisningsbeslut från Arlanda. Det bekräftar migrationsminister Johan Forssell (M). – Att få till ett fungerande återvändande till Somalia har varit särskilt prioriterat, säger han i en kommentar till Expressen. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Expressen kunde under natten rapportera att ett chartrat flygplan, med ett tiotal somaliska medborgare ombord, lyfte från Arlanda. Insatsen planerades under stort hemlighetsmakeri, enligt Expressens uppgifter. Bland annat eftersom att det i september uppstod tumult när ett reguljärflyg med personer som skulle utvisas skulle lämna Arlanda. Migrationsminister Johan Forssell (M) bekräftar nu att utvisningarna ägt rum. – Det stämmer att det har verkställts utvisningar till Somalia. Grunden för en reglerad invandring är att de beslut som fattats av myndigheter och domstolar också efterföljs, vilket också är avgörande för att vi ska lyckas med integrationen av dem som har fått ett ja, säger han i en kommentar till Expressen. Förra året stoppades en annan planerad utvisning från Sverige till Somalia efter att somaliska myndigheter satt stopp för den. – Tidigare har återvändandet till Somalia inte fungerat, vilket har inneburit att personer som inte haft rätt att vara i Sverige och inte velat följa det beslut som fattats ändå har varit kvar här. Bland dem finns både personer som har fått avslag på sina asylansökningar och personer som dömts till utvisning på grund av brott, säger Forssell. Även ombord planet som lyfte under natten fanns personer som är dömda för brott, enligt Expressens uppgifter. Däremot var det inte brottsligheten som låg bakom utvisningsbesluten, utan att personerna lämnat uppgifter som inte stämmer när de kom till Sverige, enligt uppgifterna Johan Forssell säger vidare att det har varit ”särskilt prioriterat” att få till ett fungerat återvändande till Somalia.

articles.title: Oron växer i S: Då åker vi på storstryk
articles.summary: S har inte kommit närmare att bilda regering. Nu växer frustrationen i partiet – och irritationen mot partiledningen. Tystnaden bland S-topparna är kompakt.
articles.body_text: S har inte kommit närmare att bilda regering. Nu växer frustrationen – och irritationen mot partiledningen. – Vi åker på storstryk om det blir extraval, säger en S-källa. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Inom alla de fyra rödgröna partierna stiger frustrationen över hur lite som hittills hänt i försöken att bilda en ny regering. Magdalena Andersson (S) har röstats ned som statsminister en gång, och de bilaterala samtalen fortsätter. Men några förhandlingar i fyrgrupp har inte skett och framdriften beskrivs av källor i alla fyra partier som ”i princip noll”. Irritationen är utbredd över att S inte ger några besked om vilken regering man vill bilda – samtidigt som Andersson och S-ledningen upplevs som ”initiativlös”. – Deras passivitet är slående, säger en centerpartist. Expressen har under onsdagen ringt runt i Socialdemokraterna , för att få en bild av hur partilandet upplever situationen. Totalt har ett 20-tal S-företrädare på hög nivå kontaktats, däribland partistyrelse, riksdagsgrupp och distrikt. En person har på sms avböjt att svara, ett par personer har lovat att återkomma. Bara en har svarat – Ulf Olsson, ordförande för S i Sjuhäradsbygden. – Jag hänvisar allt till Magda och Tobias, säger han. När S-toppen Lawen Redar på tisdagen får frågan om vems fel det är att Sverige ännu inte har en ny regering på plats skrattar hon först – och svarar sedan kort.

articles.title: Ilskan mot Ica – efter ändringen
articles.summary: Ica lägger ner I love eco och de ekologiska produkterna delas upp under Ica Gott liv och Ica Ekologiskt. Ekotipsets Ellinor Sirén är upprörd.
articles.body_text: – Jag blev otroligt besviken, säger Ekotipsets Ellinor Sirén. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. I sociala medier har flera kritiska röster höjts mot att Icas I love eco försvinner. Ellinor Sirén, som driver Ekotipset, är besviken över förändringen och ser det som en del av en försvagad marknadsföring av ekologiska varor. De ekologiska produkterna hamnar i stället under nya Ica Gott liv eller Ica Ekologiskt. Enligt Ica beror förändringen bland annat på nya lagkrav. Icas skrotar sitt varumärke I love eco. Det meddelade matjätten i förra veckan . Förändringen har lett till en del ilskna reaktioner i sociala medier. Ellinor Sirén, som driver det populära instagram- och bloggkontot ”Ekotipset”, är en av kritikerna. Hon reagerade starkt när hon möttes av nyheten. – Jag blev otroligt besviken. Det är ett varumärke jag och många andra uppskattat just för att det är så tydligt att det är ekologiskt! Det känns sorgligt att ett så tydligt ställningstagande för ekologiskt försvinner, säger hon. De ekologiska varorna kommer i stället att delas upp. En del produkter blir en del av det nya konceptet Ica Gott liv, som ska samla produkter som är ”hälsosamma, mer hållbara eller både och”, skriver Ica. Sortimentet ska utgå från Livsmedelsverkets kostråd. De ekologiska varor som inte platsar där – till exempel ekologiska chips och utländska bär – blir en del av Ica Ekologiskt.

articles.title: Ex-rektorn: Samma problem finns kvar
articles.summary: Tidigare Lundsbergsrektorn Anders Lundin om hur man kan få bukt med tystnadskulturen på internatskolor som Sigtuna och Lundsberg.
articles.body_text: Den tidigare Lundsbergsrektorn Anders Lundin fick sparken efter att han kritiserade en internatkultur präglad av pennalism, utfrysning och tystnad. Nu nästan 30 år senare finns samma problem fortfarande kvar, skriver han i Dagens Nyheter. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Internatskolan Lundsbergs tidigare rektor Anders Lundin fick sparken efter att ha riktat kritik mot skolan och tystnadskulturen som rådde. Samma problem finns inom internatskolorna i Sverige i dag, skriver Lundin i Dagens Nyheter. Hans förslag för att förändring är bland annat fler utbildade vuxna i elevhemmen, med nolltollerans mot kränkande beteenden mellan eleverna. Efter nya misstankar om grova brott på Sigtuna humanistiska läroverket riktas åter blickarna mot de svenska internatskolorna och kulturen inom elevhemmen. En som har erfarenhet från insidan är den tidigare Lundsbergsrektorn Anders Lundin, som ledde skolan mellan 1995 och 1999. I en text i DN skriver han att han under sina år på Lundsberg mötte både elever som han beskriver som några av de bästa ungdomar han träffat och andra som han uppfattade som ” självgoda, nedlåtande och utan moralisk resning”. Enligt den tidigare rektorn handlar en central del av problematiken om de sociala nätverk som omgärdar internatskolorna. Elever och föräldrar kan vara rädda för konsekvenserna av att bryta mot en kultur där lojalitet och tystnadskultur värderas högt. Anders Lundin beskriver också hur han själv försökte agera mot problemen under sin tid som rektor. I ett tal han höll inför terminsstart framförde han ”stark kritik mot den förljugenhet, mobbning och utfrysning som fanns på Lundsberg”. Efter talet fick han lämna jobbet.

articles.title: Två döms för sexbrott mot funktionsnedsatta
articles.summary: Ett kompisgäng misstänktes för att ha utsatt flera intellektuellt funktionsnedsatta personer för grova våldtäkter i videosamtal. Nu döms två av dem i hovrätten.
articles.body_text: Ett kompisgäng misstänktes för att ha utsatt flera intellektuellt funktionsnedsatta personer för grova våldtäkter i videosamtal. De åtta åtalade – fyra män och fyra kvinnor – frikändes i tingsrätten. Nu dömer hovrätten en 26-årig man och kvinna för sexuellt ofredande. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Under två års tid misstänktes flera intellektuellt funktionsnedsatta män och kvinnor ha utsatts för grova sexuella övergrepp och romansbedrägerier av ett kompisgäng med bas i Värmland . I ett videosamtal ska en kvinna uppmanats att föra in en feferoni och pizzabitar i sitt könsorgan. – Jag kommer hamna i helvetet. Men jag har haft roligt på jorden i alla fall, sa en av de åtalade männen under ett av övergreppen – och gapskrattar. Vid ett annat tillfälle ska kompisgänget övertalat en funktionsnedsatt man, boende på ett serviceboende i Trollhättan, att penetrera sin anal med en vattenslang. Ett annat offer uppmanades enligt utredningen att penetrera sin anal med en flaska och en osthyvel. De misstänkta övergreppen begick enligt åtalet i videosamtal via Snapchat, Facebook och Yubo, och alltid med flera deltagare. Flera av de misstänkta ska vid olika tillfällen ha varit hemma hos offren och hanterat filmningen. De åtta åtalade – män och kvinnor mellan 22 och 20 år gamla – riskerade långa fängelsestraff för grov våldtäkt och grovt sexuellt ofredande men friades i januari i år i Värmlands tingsrätt. – Vi hade förväntat oss en fällande dom avseende sexualbrotten. Det här var både överraskande och förvånande, sa kammaråklagare Lena Bohlin efter domen till Expressen. Nu ändrar hovrätten två av tingsrättens domar. En 26-årig man döms till villkorlig dom för sexuellt ofredande och bedrägeri mot en person. En 26-årig kvinna döms också till villkorlig dom för sexuellt ofredande och bedrägeri mot två personer.

articles.body_text: Dödsiffran stiger efter den stora tågolyckan i Spanien. Minst 64 personer har dött och ett hundratal skadats efter att två höghastighetståg kolliderat, rapporterar spanska medier. Spaniens transportminister menar att ett datorfel och ett ignorerat rödljus orsakat olyckan, rapporterar ABC . Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Två höghastighetståg har kolliderat i provinsen Toledo i Spanien . Olyckan inträffade strax före klockan 09 på onsdagsmorgonen på höghastighetslinjen mellan Madrid och Andalusien, i närheten av Urda söder om Madrid. Minst 64 personer har dött och närmare 80 har skadats, enligt uppgifter frånregeringskällor i regionen Castilla-La Mancha enligt flera spanska medier bland annat El Pais. Siffrorna går isär men har ökat kontinuerligt under dagen. Minst 55 personer är inlagda på sjukhus i regionen. Minst 540 personer färdades med de två tågen. Bilder från platsen visar hur flera tågvagnar har spårat ur. Minst två vagnar har kastats ner för en banvall och ligger på sidan. Det ena tåget hade lämnat Madrid på morgonen och var på väg mot Sevilla. Det andra tåget trafikerade samma sträcka. Enligt spanska medier hade det ena tåget stannat in efter problem i trafiken. Det andra körde då in i det stillastående tåget bakifrån. Spaniens transportminister Òscar Puente höll på onsdagseftermiddagen en pressträff. Han beskriver hur det bakomliggande tåget ”oförklarligt” fortsatt köra med normal hastighet, trots att trafikljuset var rött. Samtidigt ska tågets kontrollsystem LZB varit ur funktion till följd av ett datorfel.
